freeze_rule: Every threshold and case in this file is registered before the corresponding measurement runs. Measured values are recorded in verification.json only. A failing criterion is reported as a failure; it is never relaxed after the fact.

runtime.inference_mode: model(x, training=False); no Model.predict, no optimizer, compile=False on load
runtime.dtype: float32 for every model input, weight and forward output; reductions over gradients and attributions accumulate in float64
runtime.gradient_owner: same runtime - torch autograd on the Keras 3 graph. No forward-only runtime, no auxiliary runtime, no second model copy.
runtime.conversion_artifacts: none. The adopted .keras files are loaded as-is, so there is no converted-model SHA to track.
runtime.reference_runtime_for_parity: keras 3.14.1 on the tensorflow 2.21.0 backend, same .keras bytes, separate process

cases.note: Numeric probes, not biological targets. The two real windows come from the #190 demo sequences through core.scan_all; the homopolymer and alternating windows are degenerate inputs chosen to expose backend differences, and neither carries a valid PAM in the Cas12a layout.

user_default.ig_baseline: zero vector for every model input
user_default.shap_background: uniform random ACGT one-hot, numpy default_rng(seed)

finer_verification_run.purpose: Reference for resolution and background-sampling stability only. The user-facing default stays at 32 / 64 / 4 and is never raised without telling the user.

settings.cas12a_ig_inputs: The dual-input path already implemented in xai/explain.py (both Input_Seq and Input_Feat interpolated from their own zero baselines). #193 verifies only that the runtime supplies finite gradients for both inputs. Choosing between the dual-input and the composite F(x) = model(x, derive(x)) path, and that path's own completeness contract, is #195.

forward_parity.what: Same .keras bytes under the torch backend vs the tensorflow backend, inference mode, float32, every fixed case, every output head.
forward_parity.rationale: float32 eps is about 1.2e-7 and both graphs accumulate over a 30-34 step recurrence plus convolution reductions, so a few hundred eps of reordering noise is expected. 1e-4 raw is still below the 0.01 %p resolution the screen can show for the Cas12a probability, and far below the 0.5 %p a SpCas9 z-score moves per 1e-4.

layerwise_parity.what: Every layer output of both models, torch backend vs tensorflow backend, same inputs.
layerwise_parity.purpose: This is the evidence for 'same ops', including LSTM gate order and Bidirectional forward/backward halves: a transposed kernel or a swapped gate shows up as a layer-output mismatch even when the final scalar happens to agree.

weight_placement.what: Per-variable path, shape, dtype and SHA-256 of the float32 bytes, torch backend vs tensorflow backend.
weight_placement.requirement: identical variable set, identical shapes and dtypes, bitwise identical weight bytes
weight_placement.rationale: Loading must not reinterpret or transpose stored weights. Bitwise equality is the right bar here because no arithmetic happens during load.

function_match.what: The forward value the IG path returns at alpha = 1 vs the prediction forward for the same window.
function_match.rationale: Same runtime, same dtype, same graph; only batching differs, so this should be 0 up to batch-reduction order.

gradient_check.what: Autograd input gradient vs central finite differences on every model input, at the real one-hot point and at an interior interpolation point alpha = 0.5.
gradient_check.rationale: The forward is float32, so its noise floor is about 1e-6; a central difference with h = 1e-2 therefore carries about 1e-4 of noise against gradient components of order 1e-2 to 1e-0. A 2 percent relative L2 bound is what that noise allows, and cosine 0.999 catches any wrong direction, transposition or missing term.

finiteness.what: Every forward output, input gradient, IG attribution, IG completeness term, SHAP value and SHAP base value in the whole verification run.
finiteness.requirement: all finite; no NaN, no inf

ig_completeness.what: |sum(attributions) - (f(x) - f(baseline))| in raw units, at the user default 32 steps and again at 256 steps.
ig_completeness.rationale: Midpoint-rule discretization dominates here, not float noise. The bounds are set at roughly 0.5 %p of the Cas12a probability scale and at the same relative size against a z-score of order 1, which is the point where a completeness gap would start to change what the screen tells the user.

ig_resolution_stability.what: Per-position attribution at 32 steps vs 256 steps, after projection to the window positions.
ig_resolution_stability.sign_agreement: 100% on positions whose |attribution at 256 steps| is at least 0.1 * max|attribution at 256 steps|
ig_resolution_stability.purpose: Decides whether the user's 32 steps is enough, rather than assuming it.

shap_additivity.what: |base_value + sum(values) - f(x)| in raw units at the user default 64 samples / 4 backgrounds.

same_seed_determinism.what: Two runs at seed 0 with identical settings

cross_seed.what: seeds 0, 1, 2 at the user default; the background set changes with the seed

default_vs_finer.what: user default vs 512 samples / 32 backgrounds at seed 0

shap_repeat_stability.rationale: Same-seed determinism is a correctness gate. The cross-seed and finer-run bounds test whether 4 backgrounds and 64 samples are a stable enough estimate of the same quantity; they are pre-registered precisely because this is the user's current default and #191 lists it as subject to verification.

addendum_1.why: The first verification run failed `gradient_check` on 9 of 32 case/point combinations (worst: relative L2 0.264, cosine 0.969). That failure stands as recorded. These two diagnostics are registered BEFORE they run, to decide between the two explanations - a wrong autograd gradient, or central finite differences being the wrong instrument at ReLU/LeakyReLU kinks and at one-hot zeros. They do not replace or relax `gradient_check`.

cross_runtime_gradient_parity.what: Input gradient from torch autograd under the torch backend vs tf.GradientTape under the tensorflow backend, same .keras bytes, same inputs, both at x and at the interior point alpha = 0.5, every fixed case.
cross_runtime_gradient_parity.rationale: Two independent autograd implementations of the same graph. Agreement here means the gradient is right and the finite-difference comparison is the weak instrument; disagreement means the runtime choice has a real gradient problem. Bound matches forward_parity for the same float32-reordering reason.

directional_finite_difference.what: Directional derivative g . u vs central finite difference along the same unit direction u, 32 seeded random directions per case (numpy default_rng(193)), step 1e-3, at the interior point alpha = 0.5.
directional_finite_difference.rationale: A random direction averages over many coordinates, so a single kink contributes a small share of the total change, unlike a coordinate step that lands directly on one. Median plus max is reported so one kinked direction cannot hide behind the median.

kink_evidence.what: Count of ReLU/LeakyReLU pre-activation sign changes between x - h and x + h over the coordinate perturbations used by the failed gradient_check, per case.
kink_evidence.purpose: Shows directly whether the failing cases are the kinked ones.
